mainTopic: Prepared materials for כיסוי הדם on יום טוב: loose earth, stove ashes, earth brought in before יום טוב, and the כוי challenge
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how one may dig with a דקר to cover blood on יום טוב. The earth is loose (עפר תיחוח), so nothing is crushed. The hole left behind does not matter either, because following רבי אבא, a hole dug only for its earth is פטור. Next, רבה explains that the משנה's mention of stove ashes (אפר כירה) is an extra ruling: ashes also count as prepared. רב limits this, and a ברייתא backs him up. Ashes count as prepared only if the fire was lit before יום טוב, unless they are still hot enough to roast an egg. The גמרא then teaches that earth brought in before יום טוב is prepared, and רב יהודה allows a basketful to be used for all needs. מר זוטרא adds that this holds only if it was kept in a set-aside corner. Finally, the גמרא defends רב יהודה against a challenge from the כוי. It explains that the כוי case speaks of someone with no prepared earth, and that it teaches that even a doubtful obligation to cover blood is not pushed aside by שמחת יום טוב.

steps.title: The digging is in loose earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question about crushing earth: the משנה refers to loose earth that needs no crushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about loose, crumbly earth.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers a question on the previous amud. Digging with a דקר seemed to involve crushing earth, which is a forbidden מלאכה. The גמרא says the case is loose earth, so nothing is being crushed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that breaking up hard clods is like grinding (טוחן). If the earth is already loose, there is no crushing at all. That removes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered animal or bird

phrases.english: With loose earth.
phrases.notes: Answers the prior question about crushing (כותש).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the crushing question raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Digging with a דקר involves crushing clods.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is loose earth, so no crushing happens.

steps.title: But he is still making a hole
steps.stepSummary: Even with loose earth, removing it leaves a hole, and making a hole is a forbidden מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is making a hole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. Even if no crushing happens, taking earth out leaves a pit in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging a hole falls under building or plowing. So solving the crushing problem leaves a second problem: the hole itself.

phrases.english: But he is making a hole!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that digging loose earth on יום טוב is fine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing earth creates a hole, which is itself a forbidden act.

steps.title: Following רבי אבא, an unwanted hole brings no liability
steps.stepSummary: Someone who digs only for the earth, not for the hole, is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי אבא, who said: one who digs a hole on שבת but only needs its earth is exempt for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the hole challenge. It brings רבי אבא's rule that a hole you don't want is not counted against you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The digger wants the earth, not the pit, so the hole is a damaging act (מקלקל), not a constructive one. A מקלקל is פטור. So the hole does not make covering the blood forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא whose rule is cited
one who damages rather than builds

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle across הלכות שבת: an act done only for a side result, where the main 'product' is unwanted damage, does not bring liability.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Abba.
As Rabbi Abba said:
One who digs a hole on Shabbat,
and needs only its earth,
is exempt for it.
phrases.notes: He does not want the hole, so it counts as damage, not building.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making any hole is a forbidden מלאכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hole you don't need, dug only for its earth, is פטור.
steps.whatToRemember: Digging for loose earth to cover blood on יום טוב is fine. There is no crushing because the earth is loose, and the hole is unwanted, following רבי אבא.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about stove ashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that stove ashes are prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the ashes of a stove are prepared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה. This is a setup line: it quotes the words so it can question them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says בית הלל agree that if one already slaughtered, he may dig and cover. It then adds 'because stove ashes are prepared.' The גמרא is about to ask why ashes come up at all.

phrases.english: For the ashes of a stove are prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a different phrase of the משנה.

steps.title: Who mentioned ashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה suddenly mentions stove ashes, since nothing earlier discussed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled. The משנה gives a reason about ashes, but the case was about digging earth, not ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שֶׁ' ('because') makes the ashes sound like the reason for the earlier ruling. But ashes have nothing to do with digging with a דקר. The wording seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: who mentioned its name? (it came up out of nowhere)

phrases.english: The ashes of a stove, who mentioned them?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ashes were never part of the case, so they cannot be the reason for it.

steps.title: רבה: read it as 'and also stove ashes are prepared'
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the משנה is adding a new point: stove ashes also count as prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said, this is what it means: 'And stove ashes are prepared.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה fixes the reading. The ashes are not a reason. They are an additional ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'because,' read 'and.' Besides prepared earth, stove ashes are also ready to use for כיסוי הדם without being set aside the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who explains the משנה

phrases.english: Rabba said, this is what it is saying:
And the ashes of a stove are prepared.
phrases.notes: 'And,' meaning an additional rule, not a reason.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ashes are given as the reason for digging.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ashes are a separate rule: they also count as prepared.

steps.title: רב: ashes count only if the stove was lit before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the rule. Ashes are prepared only if the fire was lit on ערב יום טוב. Ashes formed on יום טוב are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They only taught this when the stove was lit on ערב יום טוב. But if it was lit on יום טוב, the ashes are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a limit to the משנה's ruling about stove ashes. It depends on when the fire was lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes that already existed when יום טוב began were available, so they are prepared. Ashes that came into being on יום טוב are new (נולד) and count as מוקצה, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: the student who passes on רב's teaching
they only taught this when (a limiting formula)
something newly created on the holy day (a type of מוקצה)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּסַּק מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: They only taught this when it was lit on the Festival eve,
but if it was lit on the Festival, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבה's reading of the ashes rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ashes are prepared only if the fire was lit before יום טוב. Ashes made on יום טוב are forbidden.

steps.title: Exception: ashes hot enough to roast an egg
steps.stepSummary: Even ashes from a fire lit on יום טוב are allowed if they are still hot enough to roast an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they are fit to roast an egg in them, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds an exception to his own limit. Hot ashes are still useful, so they are not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes that can still cook an egg are part of a usable fire, not new, useless leftovers. Since they are clearly fit for use, they are not מוקצה and may be used to cover the blood.
steps.confusionAlert: This exception applies only to ashes from a fire lit on יום טוב. Ashes from a fire lit before יום טוב are allowed even when cold.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָאוּי לִצְלוֹת בּוֹ בֵּיצָה — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And if it is fit to roast an egg in it, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Exception to the ban on ashes formed on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot ashes that can roast an egg are permitted even if formed on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Stove ashes may be used for כיסוי הדם on יום טוב if the fire was lit before יום טוב. If the fire was lit on יום טוב, they may be used only while still hot enough to roast an egg.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the rule about stove ashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches exactly what רב said. Stove ashes are prepared only if the fire was lit on ערב יום טוב, and ashes from a fire lit on יום טוב are allowed only if they are hot enough to roast an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא: When they said stove ashes are prepared, they meant only when the fire was lit on ערב יום טוב. If it was lit on יום טוב, the ashes are forbidden. But if they are still hot enough to roast an egg, they are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב, giving his rule outside support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 8 gave the rule as רב's own words. Now a ברייתא, which is an older teaching from the time of the משנה, states both parts: the ערב יום טוב condition and the hot-enough-to-roast-an-egg exception. This shows רב was not adding something new on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Also like this. Signals support for the previous statement
Was lit or heated (the stove fire)
Hot enough to roast an egg in it

steps.whatToRemember: Stove ashes are prepared if the fire was lit on ערב יום טוב. Ashes formed on יום טוב are forbidden unless they are still hot enough to roast an egg. A ברייתא confirms this.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way (in a baraita):
When they said that stove ashes are prepared,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּסַּק מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: they said it only when the stove was lit on the eve of the Festival;
but if it was lit on the Festival, the ashes are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָאוּי לִצְלוֹת בּוֹ בֵּיצָה — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And if they are hot enough to roast an egg in them, they are permitted.
phrases.notes: Hot ashes are usable for cooking, so they were never set aside as unusable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rules of steps 7 and 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's limitation (prepared only if lit on ערב יום טוב) and the egg-roasting exception.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states both parts of the rule word for word.

steps.title: Earth brought into a garden or ruin may be used for covering
steps.stepSummary: If someone brought earth into his garden or ruin before יום טוב, he may use it to cover blood on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone brought earth into his garden or his ruin before יום טוב, it is permitted to cover blood with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from ashes to earth. It teaches that earth deliberately brought into one's own property counts as prepared for כיסוי הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary loose earth outdoors is not set aside for use, so it is מוקצה on יום טוב. When a person brings earth into his garden or ruin before יום טוב, he has shown he plans to use it, so it counts as prepared. He may then use it to cover blood after slaughtering a חיה or bird.

keyTerms.meaning: To cover (here, the blood of a slaughtered חיה or bird)

phrases.english: If one brought earth into his garden or his ruin (before the Festival),
it is permitted to cover (blood) with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from prepared ashes to prepared earth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth brought into one's garden or ruin before יום טוב counts as prepared and may be used for כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a basketful of earth may be used for all needs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person may bring a basketful of earth home before יום טוב and use it for anything he needs on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: A person may bring in a basketful of earth and use it for all his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a similar rule. Earth brought in a basket before יום טוב is ready for any use on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing the earth in on purpose before יום טוב makes it prepared, just like the garden case in step 10. רב יהודה goes further: it can be used for all needs, not only for covering blood.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
A person may bring in a full basket of earth (before the Festival)
and use it for all his needs (on the Festival).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא's ruling in line with step 10, extending it to all uses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basketful of earth brought in before יום טוב is prepared for every use on יום טוב.

steps.title: מר זוטרא limits the rule to earth set aside in a corner
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting מר זוטרא רבה, says רב יהודה's rule applies only if the person set aside a corner for the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught publicly in the name of מר זוטרא רבה: This applies only if he set aside a corner for it.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds a condition to רב יהודה's rule. The earth counts as prepared only if it is kept in its own corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the earth is just spread around the floor, it becomes part of the ground and is no longer something separate to use. Piling it in a set-aside corner shows the person is keeping it for later use. Only then does it count as prepared.
steps.confusionAlert: The corner is the condition that makes the earth allowed. Earth that is just scattered on the floor is the case that is not allowed, because it becomes part of the floor.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught publicly
in the name of Mar Zutra the Great:
And that is only when he designated a corner for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא רַבָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth brought in counts as prepared only when it is kept in a designated corner.

steps.title: Challenge from the כוי: why not cover its blood with prepared earth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a משנה: a כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, and if it was, its blood is not covered. But with רב יהודה's prepared earth, why not cover it?
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, and if one slaughtered it, its blood is not covered. But if רב יהודה is right, let him cover it with prepared earth, as רב יהודה said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה using the case of a כוי. If prepared earth may be used for anything, why does the משנה say not to cover a כוי's blood?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי is an animal we are unsure about: it might be a חיה, whose blood must be covered, or a בהמה, whose blood need not be covered. Covering for a doubtful reason would normally not justify handling earth on יום טוב. But if earth from רב יהודה's basket is fully usable, covering costs nothing, so the משנה's ban seems to contradict רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
An animal of uncertain status, between a חיה and a בהמה
And if it is so (if that view were correct)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי, אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: A koy: one may not slaughter it on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שְׁחָטוֹ — אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶת דָּמוֹ.
phrases.english: and if one slaughtered it, one does not cover its blood.
And if it is so (as Rav Yehuda says),
let him cover it, in accordance with Rav Yehuda!
phrases.notes: That is, with the prepared basket of earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's ruling from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that a prepared basket of earth may be used for all needs on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If prepared earth is freely usable, there is no reason to forbid covering a כוי's blood. Yet the משנה forbids it, which suggests prepared earth is not freely usable.

steps.title: The ruling must speak about someone who has no prepared earth
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge could be raised from stove ashes or an embedded shovel. So the ruling about the כוי must refer to someone who has no prepared covering at all, and that would include רב יהודה's basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, you could also ask: let him cover the blood with stove ashes, or with earth loosened by a shovel already stuck in the ground! Rather, the case is where he does not have these. Here too, the case is where he does not have a prepared basket of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב יהודה. It points out that the same question could be asked using other permitted materials, so the case must be where the person has nothing prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without רב יהודה, there are well-known permitted ways to cover blood on יום טוב: אפר כירה and earth from a דקר נעוץ. If the ruling about the כוי still forbids covering, it must be speaking about someone who has none of these. So it also speaks about someone who has no basket of earth, and רב יהודה's rule is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning the questioner's logic back on him)
A shovel or spade stuck into the ground before יום טוב; the earth it loosens may be used
That he does not have (any prepared material)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a כוי's blood can never be covered with prepared earth. It is saying the ruling describes a specific situation: a person who has nothing prepared.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
phrases.notes: Shows the challenge proves too much.

phrases.english: let him cover it with stove ashes,
phrases.notes: Stove ashes from a fire lit before יום טוב are prepared (Step 9).

phrases.english: or with earth loosened by an embedded shovel!
Rather, it is a case where he does not have these,
here too, it is a case where he does not have a basket of earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 against רב יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the source speaks of someone with no prepared covering material.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling about the כוי seemed to apply even to someone who had a prepared basket of earth, which would contradict רב יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling applies only to someone with no prepared material at all, so רב יהודה stands.

steps.title: Then why mention a doubtful animal at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is someone without prepared earth, then even a definite wild animal or bird could not be slaughtered. So why does the source single out the כוי, which is a doubtful case?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why speak specifically about a doubtful case? Even a definite case would also not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the person has no earth, the doubtful status of the כוי seems irrelevant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows בית הלל: a person may not slaughter a חיה or bird on יום טוב unless he has prepared earth to cover the blood. So if the case is someone with no earth, even an animal whose blood must definitely be covered could not be slaughtered. Choosing the doubtful כוי as the example then seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is correct)
A doubt; here the כוי, whose blood may or may not need covering
Definite; an animal whose blood certainly must be covered

phrases.english: If so,
why speak specifically about a doubtful case,
phrases.notes: The כוי is a doubtful animal.

phrases.english: even a definite case would also not be allowed!
phrases.notes: Without prepared earth, one may not slaughter even a definite חיה or bird.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the source speaks of someone with no prepared earth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no earth, the doubt about the כוי makes no difference, since even a definite animal could not be slaughtered. So why mention a doubtful case?

steps.title: The source teaches that even the doubtful case is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The source uses a 'it goes without saying' style. A definite animal obviously may not be slaughtered without earth. One might have thought that a doubtful one may be slaughtered for the joy of יום טוב, leaving its blood uncovered, so the source teaches that this is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It speaks in the style of 'it goes without saying': It goes without saying that a definite animal may not be slaughtered. But for a doubtful one, I might say: because of the joy of יום טוב, let him slaughter it and not cover its blood. So the source teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the doubtful case was chosen. The definite case is obvious, and the real new lesson is about the doubtful case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since covering a כוי's blood is only a doubtful obligation, one might think שמחת יום טוב outweighs it. Then he could slaughter and simply skip the covering. The source rules out that idea: even for a doubtful animal, one may not slaughter on יום טוב without prepared earth. This completes the defense of רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It speaks in the style of 'it goes without saying' (the obvious case is assumed, and the less obvious case is the lesson)
The מצוה to rejoice on יום טוב, such as by eating meat
I might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling about the כוי refers to someone with no prepared earth, so רב יהודה's basket is not contradicted. The כוי is mentioned to teach that even a doubtful obligation to cover blood is not pushed aside by שמחת יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a doubtful מצוה of covering blood is still taken seriously. One may not create a situation on יום טוב where the blood will be left uncovered.

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'it goes without saying':
it goes without saying that a definite animal may not be slaughtered,
but a doubtful one,
I might say that because of the joy of the Festival
let him slaughter it and not cover its blood,
phrases.notes: The doubtful obligation to cover the blood might seem to give way to שמחת יום טוב.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that he may not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: 'לא מבעיא' style: the obvious case is assumed, and the lesson is in the less obvious case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For a doubtful animal, שמחת יום טוב might permit slaughtering and leaving the blood uncovered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a doubtful animal may not be slaughtered on יום טוב without prepared earth, so the example teaches something new.
